regime.label: Dealer long-gamma cushion collapses 95% as the future breaks 1.7 points below the 1060 gamma hinge
evidence: Net dealer GEX is +199 today versus +3,914 five sessions ago (25 Aug) and +2,762 yesterday, a 95% collapse that leaves the book gamma-neutral in aggregate and removes the damping that held the 1065-1075 chop.

Spot 1058.3 sits 1.7 points below the 1060 hinge: per-strike net GEX is -2,424 at 1050 and -1,921 at 1030 against +2,898 at 1080 and +2,285 at 1100, so hedging amplifies below and dampens above (the cumulative sum only crosses zero at 1140 on thin far-OTM call OI, so 1060 is the working flip).

Put OI at 1020 built +476 over five sessions (+202 today) on 325 lots traded while ATM IV expanded to 14.09% from the 13.00% low on 26 Aug: volume plus OI build plus IV move plus price approaching is a live Vol2Vol confirmation, not stale OI.
Max pain drifted 10 points down to 1060 and the flip migrated 1080 to 1060 over five sessions, tracking a 14.8-point (-1.4%) slide in the future from 1073.1.

S50U26.today_summary: 1058.3 on the front future, down 6.7 points on the day and 14.8 points (-1.4%) over five sessions, now 1.7 points below the 1060 gamma hinge and sitting on max pain at 1060. Net dealer GEX is +199 against +3,914 five sessions ago, a 95% collapse that strips out the long-gamma damping that contained the prior week's range. Put/call OI is 2.14 (41,712 put lots vs 19,536 call lots) but today's flow turned call-heavy at 0.87 P/C volume, with +271 call lots of OI added at 1070 and +202 put lots at 1020. ATM IV 14.09% is the highest of the last six sessions, up 1.09 points off the 13.00% low, with 25-delta skew put-rich at +1.98.
what_changed: Net GEX fell to +199 from +2,762 yesterday and +3,914 on 25 Aug, the largest one-day erosion in the window, as the gamma-weighted strikes slid onto the put-heavy 1030-1050 rows (1050 put OI 1,830 vs call OI 794).
Gamma flip migrated to 1060 from 1070 yesterday and 1080 on 25-26 Aug, and the future closed below it for the first time in the six-session window.
Max pain slipped 10 points to 1060 from 1070, so the anchor now sits 1.7 points above spot instead of 5.6 points above.
P/C volume dropped to 0.87 from 1.39 as call volume rose 51% to 2,564: call OI added +271 at 1070, +159 at 1110 and +121 at 1060 while put OI added +202 at 1020 and +108 at 1030.
S50U26.five_day_thesis: The future has fallen 14.8 points from 1073.1 on 25 Aug to 1058.3 and every structural marker followed it down: max pain 1070 to 1060, gamma flip 1080 to 1060, and 25-delta skew widening from +0.13 to a +2.90 peak on 2 Sep before easing to +1.98 today. The decisive change is the net-GEX path 3,914, 5,536, 2,019, 3,492, 2,762, 199: dealers carried a long-gamma cushion through the 1065-1075 chop and no longer do, because the high-gamma strikes have migrated onto put-heavy rows. OI is building rather than unwinding, with put OI up 2,365 (+6%) and call OI up 1,112 (+6%) over five sessions, +476 put lots at 1020 and +335 at the 910 structural floor (now 16,227 lots), so this is protection stacking, not a position being closed. ATM IV expanded 1.09 points off the 13.00% low as price fell, the opposite of the compression that normally accompanies a quiet drift into max pain. The 1060-1080 corridor is the boundary: above it dealer hedging dampens into the 1100 call wall (2,780 lots, +2,285 GEX), below it hedging amplifies with no positive-GEX shelf until the 1020/1000 put build.

strategies.name: Put debit spread 1040 / 1010
strategies.rationale: Expresses the short-gamma break directly: net GEX is -2,424 at 1050 and -1,456 at 1040, so a move through the 1050 near-put wall forces dealers to sell into weakness rather than fade it, and 1σ daily of 9.39 points reaches 1040 in a single session.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit, roughly 5.9 points at mid (9.9 - 4.0); max gain 24.1 points, breakeven 1034.1.
strategies.invalidation: A daily close back above the 1060 gamma flip, and decisively above 1070 where net GEX turns +1,031.

strategies.name: Call credit spread 1080 / 1100
strategies.rationale: Sells into the one part of the book where dealers remain long gamma and will dampen a rally: net GEX is +2,898 at 1080 and +2,285 at 1100, with the 1100 call wall the largest OI in the chain at 2,780 lots, and 1080 is exactly the 25-delta call band.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = 20 - net credit, roughly 15.65 points at mid (credit 4.35); breakeven 1084.35.
strategies.invalidation: A close above the 1100 call wall, which would put spot beyond the +39.8-point 1σ expiry band and negate the long-gamma ceiling.

strategies.name: Put debit spread 1020 / 990 (tail)
strategies.rationale: Cheap expression of the acceleration tail below the protection shelf: 1σ to the 29 Sep expiry is 39.8 points (1018.5), the +476-lot five-day OI build at 1020 is where dealer short-gamma hedging is densest below spot, and put IV at 1020 is 16.19% against 14.09% ATM.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit, roughly 2.45 points at mid (5.2 - 2.75); max gain 27.55 points, breakeven 1017.55.
strategies.invalidation: A close above 1060 with net GEX rebuilding above +2,000, which restores the damping regime this structure is paid for losing.

S50U26.prediction: Base case is a 1018.5-1098.1 range into the 29 Sep expiry (1σ = 39.8 points over 18 trading sessions), with the near-term bias tilted lower while the future holds below the 1060 flip: the first air pocket is 1050-1040 where net GEX reads -2,424 and -1,456, and 1σ daily is 9.39 points. A daily close above 1070 restores the positive-GEX shelf (+1,031 at 1070, +2,898 at 1080) and invalidates the downside-acceleration read, making the 1080-1100 call wall the more likely magnet. Below 1020 the +476-lot five-day put build becomes the next structural shelf.
S50U26.risk_note: Educational analysis only, not trade advice. SET50 options are European and cash-settled on the SET50 index, so there is no physical delivery and no share-settlement mechanic to force price toward a strike: pinning near max pain 1060 is a tendency, not a guarantee, and is structurally weaker here than for physically-settled single stocks. With 26 days to expiry and net GEX at only +199, the pin argument is weak in any case; the active risk is the opposite one, that real flow beats the option structure. Defined-risk is not risk-free, and the short-vol leg above carries the negative-skew payoff profile of small frequent gains against a rare 15.65-point loss.
